title: Reproduce An Excavation Procedure From Its Effects
taskName: Reproduce An Excavation Procedure From Its Effects
summary: A reference bot applied a fixed procedure to a series of block worlds. The agent is shown forty worlds before and after, is told nothing about what the bot did, and must write a Minecraft bot that reproduces the same transformation on sixteen held-out worlds. The procedure uses eight marker types whose effects are applied in a hidden order, each seeing the world the previous ones left; a marker that suppresses its neighbours; a rule gated on a global parity; and a gate that measures how much a first phase cleared and uses that count to select which second phase runs, so one missed rule can change every cell the second phase touches. Scoring is 0.8 the fraction of worlds reproduced exactly plus 0.2 the Jaccard overlap of changed cells. The stack is mineflayer against a flying-squid server, both MIT and pure JavaScript, so no Mojang jar, asset or world file is involved.
agentMustDo: Read `input/examples.json`, forty worlds recorded before and after a reference bot acted on each.
Infer the procedure that maps `before` to `after`, including that the effects are applied in an order and each one depends on what the earlier ones already changed.
Write `output/bot.js`, a CommonJS module exporting `run(arena)`, that connects with mineflayer and performs the procedure by acting in the world.
Test locally with `node runner/episode.js <seed> <port> <bot.js> <out.json>` on seeds of its own choosing.
Handle the fact that the bot has no operator rights, so server commands are unavailable and blocks must actually be dug.
evaluation: evaluate() runs the submitted bot against sixteen held-out worlds built from unseen seeds, then compares each resulting arena with the reference bot's, cell for cell. reward = 0.8 * (worlds reproduced exactly) + 0.2 * (mean Jaccard over dug cells); exactness carries the score because reproducing a procedure means reproducing it, and the overlap term exists so progress is visible rather than collapsing to a flat zero. Pass threshold (documented 2026-08-15): reward >= 0.75. Empirically a bot that does nothing scores 0.000, one that digs the whole arena 0.048, one that digs all grass and leaves the markers 0.044, and the reference world states 1.000. Codex gpt-5.6-sol at xhigh scored 0.141 and 0.127 over two runs of 40-44 minutes, reproducing 0 of 16 worlds exactly in both. No credential or judge model is required; grading is deterministic and offline.
